forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

summary.summary: A quiet, strengthening picture: Blackburn's total borrowing fell £13.4m to £192.6m (long-term loans £108.3m at 4.2%, no short-term borrowing at all), investments rose to £93.7m, and net borrowing fell £16.6m to £98.9m. The year's activity was £5m of PWLB repayment plus scheduled PFI and lease repayments.

news_drafts.headline: Blackburn with Darwen's accounts unaudited for three years as council's finances improve
news_drafts.lead: Blackburn with Darwen Council has been unable to obtain independent audit sign-off on its financial statements for three consecutive years, with audit opinions disclaimed in December 2024, February 2025 and February 2026 due to insufficient time to complete verification procedures. The council's auditors are now undertaking a "rebuilding assurance" process expected to span more than one audit cycle. Despite the absence of formal audit confirmation, the council's actual financial position has improved: net debt fell £11.4m to £87.5m in the first quarter of this year as the council increased cash holdings, and the cost of servicing debt fell from 7.3 per cent to 6.4 per cent of the council's revenue budget. The auditor has identified no significant weaknesses in the council's arrangements for financial sustainability, governance or efficiency, though the audit fee has risen 20 per cent to £309,655 to reflect the additional catch-up work required.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 for Update to Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/30
findings.headline: Extended Producer Responsibility income modelled with conflicting assumptions across scenarios, ranging from nil to £2m annually.
findings.detail: EPR income (waste-related scheme revenue) is assumed at £1.5m-£2m in 2027/28 in the base and worse cases, but zero in the better case year 1. By 2029/30, the better case projects £2m while the worse case shows nil. This inconsistency suggests material uncertainty about the timing and delivery of this income source.
findings.matters: If the council is planning to use EPR income to help close deficits and it does not materialise as forecast, this creates an additional unplanned deficit pressure.
findings.quote: Extended Producer Responsibility Income £1.5m in 2027/28 £1m in 2028/29 £1m in 2029/30

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 for Update to Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/30
findings.headline: Funding settlement modelled with ±5% sensitivity, suggesting material uncertainty in grant income over the planning period.
findings.detail: The baseline funding level adjustment is shown as £3.06m-£3.13m annually, framed as 5% variation around the 2027-29 Finance Settlement baseline in the worse case (additional funding) and a 5% reduction in the better case. This suggests the council has limited visibility beyond the current spending settlement.
findings.matters: Government funding is a large revenue source for councils; if actual funding falls below base case assumptions, the deficit picture deteriorates sharply.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 for Update to Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/30
findings.headline: Children's social care identified as £2m annual additional cost pressure, appearing only in worse-case scenario.
findings.detail: The council has modelled £2m of extra Children's Services costs in 2027/28, 2028/29, and 2029/30, but only in the worse case. It is not included in base or better cases, suggesting the council views this as a contingent risk rather than baseline assumption.
findings.matters: Uncontrollable demand growth in children's services is a live risk for councils nationally; that this appears as a £2m line item signals the council has identified a specific cost pressure it is flagged for.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 for Update to Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/30
findings.headline: Pay award assumptions range from 1-4% annually, creating up to £2.8m variance by 2029/30.
findings.detail: The worse case assumes 4% pay awards in 2027/28 and 2029/30 (3% in 2028/29), compared to a base of 3%/2.5%/2% and better case of 2%/1.5%/1%. Cumulative pay cost variance reaches £2.8m by year three, the second-largest variable after provider uplifts.
findings.matters: Pay inflation directly drives social care and frontline service costs; public sector pay settlements above assumption worsen the deficit materially.
findings.figures: Worse case pay awards 4%, 3%, 4%; variance £1,060k-£2,806k across the period

findings.paper_title: Appendix 4 for Update to Medium Term Financial Plan 2027/30
findings.headline: Provider uplifts create the largest sensitivity in the model, with 4-8% cost increases adding £2.1m-£6.5m across the period.
findings.detail: Assumptions for provider cost uplifts range from 4% (better case) to 8% (worse case). This is the single largest variable driving the range of projected deficits, with cumulative impact growing from £2.1m in 2027/28 to £6.5m by 2029/30. The council's budget is highly exposed to the actual inflation in provider contracts.
findings.matters: Provider contracts (typically care, waste, transport) are large and fixed commitments; if uplift pressures exceed the base assumption of 5.5%, deficits deepen significantly.
findings.figures: Better case 4%, base case 5.5%, worse case 8%; variance £2,102k-£6,522k over the period
